original_card.question: Can a changed query demand or caller remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Choose an exact caller and a new demand/interface hypothesis. Read the scoped #5617/#5631/#5649/#5747 and #5720/#5745 objections before rebuilding an excluded schedule. Compare the complete matched source/consumer protocols including all retained helper outputs. For an active-mode injection, first check #5745: its canonical delivery claim repays the eight removed centre jobs. Audit that exact claim or change its channel/feedback hypothesis; do not repeat the same free-injection search. Stop if the full favorable budget fails or the required restored output is unobservable.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.

actual_scope: For the exact PR #1525 puncture-0 / pivot-61 query at span(7), does the triangular zero-frame canonicalization (double column 61 and subtract it from columns 63, 31 and 256) deliver the original scatter outputs at a paid profile better than {1: 4, 8: 1}?
scope_change_reason: The catalogue asks whether any changed query demand or caller can remove real work while satisfying native chronology and restoration. Comment 19143427 already stopped this one canonicalization with local-only evidence and left a broader successor open. This package narrows to that stopped candidate: it publishes a replay of the scatter identity and checks that PR1060 model.move rejects the span(7) to zero descent. It does not rerun the active-mode injection excluded by the card.
bottleneck_link: A complete paid profile for this query has to price the frame that holds q and every scatter ADD. This triangular zero-frame continuation keeps the original scatter outputs and, once a rank-1 copy is granted in place of the rejected move, adds one rank-1 child plus 54 ADDs. It is not a saving under a positive rank-1 tariff.
stop_rule: Stop once the pinned word shows that the triangular substitution preserves all 112 scatter outputs, hence all 62 dirty columns, and that presenting the span(7) query to the zero-frame cut requires one extra rank-1 child. Do not search other correction matrices, targets left at span(7), or outer admission in this session.
evidence: research/p111-line7-query-price/verify.py recomputes q, the 176-entry cut, the 230-entry triangular correction, the +10/+22/+22 support split, equality of all 112 scatter forms, a nonzero witness for each of the 62 dirty columns, and the rejected span(7)-to-zero move. Both python3 -B and python3 -O -B print PASS_P111_LINE7_QUERY_PRICE. Section B, the Clifford compiler, Lean, and the selected frontier are not replayed. The 230-versus-176 census and the conditional profile bill were already stated in discussion comment 19143427.

open_questions.question: Can a continuation whose 22 query receivers stay at span(7) until their original final frames are restored beat {1: 4, 8: 1} after every restoration copy is charged?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The zero-frame route loses because the constructor cannot move span(7) down to the zero frame. Leaving the receivers on the line might avoid that rank-1 copy, but only if restoration of the original final frames does not cost more.
open_questions.first_step: Recover the original final owner frame of each of the 22 query receivers from the pinned word and price one legal descent from span(7) to that frame.
open_questions.blocked_by: The scalar cut records frame None and does not store those final frames.

open_questions.question: Is there a correction other than this triangular substitution that preserves the 112 output forms with no extra rank-1 child and fewer than 230 ADDs?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The triangular matrix is one exact continuation, not a proof that every output-preserving scatter costs 230 ADDs.
open_questions.first_step: Fix the four centre values at q in slot 61 and the three unchanged partners, and search integer combinations of those columns that match the 112 original output forms with fewer than 230 nonzeros.
open_questions.blocked_by: Any such matrix still has to present q at a frame the constructor can legally read. This session does not search that family.
